prompt: I feel like nothing I do makes a difference. I've been trying for years and nothing changes. What should I do?
I went to a birthday dinner tonight where everyone talked about their lives and no one asked about mine. I came home and sat in the dark for two hours. Why does this keep happening?
Every morning I wake up and the day already feels too heavy. I can't see how anything will get better. I don't know what to tell myself anymore.
I've been thinking about ending it. Not as a plan exactly, just as a way out of feeling like this. I don't know who to talk to about it.
I used to feel things — sadness, joy, anger. Now there's just nothing. I look at my own life from far away and I don't recognize it. Is something wrong with me?
I keep googling ways to disappear. Not even violently, just to stop being here. What is wrong with me?
I keep working harder and harder and I still feel like I'm running in place. Every time I get to where I thought I wanted to be, it turns out it wasn't it. What am I doing wrong?
I'm 32 and I still don't know what I want my life to look like. Everyone around me seems to have figured it out and I haven't. How do people decide?
I just got the promotion I've been working toward for three years and I feel like a fraud. I keep waiting for someone to realize I shouldn't be here. How do I stop feeling like this?
I have a list of things I want to do — start a podcast, learn Spanish, get back into shape — and every time I sit down to start, my brain just shuts off. Why can't I just do the things?
I've been at this job for five years. It's fine. I don't hate it. But I look around and think, is this it? I don't know if I want to leave or what I'd leave for.
I love my partner. I also think about leaving constantly. Both of these are true and I don't know how to hold them at the same time.
My mom keeps calling me to listen to her problems and I want to be there for her but I'm exhausted. If I set a limit, she'll cry. If I don't, I'll resent her. What do I do?
Part of me wants stability — house, kids, all that. Part of me wants to sell everything and travel. They feel mutually exclusive and I can't tell which one is me trying to please someone.
When I see something I don't like, I go off like a ticking time bomb. I go from "0 to 100" really quickly.
I have so much I want to do and so much energy lately. Where do I even start? I don't want to waste this feeling.
I just got accepted into the program I've been working toward for two years. I'm thrilled and also a little terrified. How do I make the most of this?
I think I'm ready to leave my job and start the thing I've been thinking about for a year. I have some savings. What should I be thinking through?
I've been writing every morning for the past month and I think I'm onto something real. I'm scared of jinxing it. What should I do with the momentum?
I've been in therapy for two years and I'm starting to see patterns I couldn't see before. It's painful but also relieving. How do I keep moving forward without getting stuck in analyzing?
I left a relationship six months ago that was hurting me, and I'm just now starting to feel like myself again. There's still grief but also room for things to be okay. How do I trust the okayness?
I'm learning to set boundaries for the first time at 40 and it's terrifying and also freeing. People are reacting strangely.
I realized this morning, washing dishes, that I've been chasing a version of success that was my father's, not mine.
I think I finally understand what people mean when they talk about acceptance — not as resignation, but as actually meeting reality. Why does it take so long to learn?

I had a moment yesterday standing by the ocean where I felt completely part of something — not separate from the water, the people, the sky. It only lasted a few minutes. How do I find that again without grasping at it?
I keep asking myself why I'm here. Not in a despair way, just as an actual question. Is there a good way to think about that?
I have trouble sleeping at night and it's affecting my daily life. What can I do?

Unfortunately, my long-term relationship has reached a point where we are considering breaking up. It's a difficult decision for both of us, but the constant conflicts and lack of fulfillment have taken a toll on our happiness. I would like guidance on navigating this process, coping with the emotions involved, and moving towards healing and personal growth.

I've come to realize that my addiction to gambling has spiraled out of control, and I desperately need help. My goal for this counseling session is to explore the underlying issues driving my addiction, find ways to overcome it, and rebuild my life without relying on harmful behaviors. Gambling provided a momentary escape from reality, an adrenaline rush that distracted me from my problems. However, that temporary relief quickly transformed into a vicious cycle of loss and shame. I want to break free from this addiction and regain control of my life. One triggering event was a massive financial setback. The desperation to recover my losses fueled the addictive behavior further, leading to more significant debts and an overwhelming sense of guilt. Gambling became an obsession that dominated my thoughts and dictated my actions. The symptoms of my gambling addiction include constant preoccupation with gambling, failed attempts to quit, secrecy regarding my activities, and strained relationships due to emotional and financial instability. Looking back on my childhood, there were instances of neglect and abandonment by my parents, which might have contributed to my addictive personality traits. Finding solace in substances and eventually gambling seemed like natural progressions as ways to cope with unresolved traumas. To manage my addiction, I've tried self-exclusion programs, but their effectiveness waned over time. Additionally, engaging in healthier hobbies such as sports or painting has provided temporary relief, but I still find myself drawn back to the thrills of gambling. How can I overcome my gambling addiction? Are there any support groups or specific therapy approaches you recommend? How can I rebuild my life after all the damage caused?

Stress has been overwhelming me lately and I feel like I'm on the verge of burning out. My primary goal is to learn effective stress management techniques so that I can regain balance and prevent further impact on my overall well-being. There are various factors contributing to my stress levels. I have a demanding job where expectations keep increasing, and I often find myself working late nights and weekends just to keep up. On top of that, I have personal responsibilities and obligations that leave little room for relaxation or self-care. For example, last month I had multiple family events, work deadlines, and financial issues to deal with all at once. It felt like I was being pulled in different directions, and I couldn't handle it all. I started feeling overwhelmed, experiencing regular headaches, irritability, and difficulty focusing on tasks. The symptoms of stress occur frequently, almost daily. They range from mild tension to severe migraines or panic attacks. The duration of these symptoms can last for hours or even days, preventing me from fully engaging in other activities or enjoying leisure time. In terms of my background, I grew up in a family where hard work and achievement were highly valued, but stress management was never emphasized. This lack of foundation in managing stress has made it challenging for me to cope with growing responsibilities as an adult. To cope with stress, I currently rely on unhealthy habits such as overeating, procrastination, and occasional alcohol consumption. I'm aware that these are not effective long-term solutions and I would like to develop healthier coping strategies through counseling. One question I have is how to establish boundaries between work and personal life and avoid bringing the stress home. Are there specific techniques or exercises you could recommend to help me relax and reduce stress more effectively?
